title: Construction of the Great Pyramid of Khufu
summary: Egypt's 4th Dynasty king Khufu built the Great Pyramid at Giza as his tomb, in a reign Egypt's antiquities ministry dates to about 2589–2566 BCE. A core of local limestone was faced with fine Tura limestone, and the ministry estimates the work took 10 to 20 years.

uncertainty.note: Dates follow the reign of Khufu as given by Egypt's Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities; absolute Old Kingdom chronology is uncertain by a few decades, and the build time (10 to 20 years) is an estimate.

as_recorded.value: Khufu c.2589–2566 BC; construction estimated at 10 to 20 years

as_recorded.calendar: Egyptian civil calendar, Khufu regnal count
as_recorded.value: Fitting of Tura limestone cladding under way in the year after the 13th census of Khufu (Year 26), July to November

where.historical_name: Akhet-Khufu, the Horizon of Khufu, royal necropolis near Memphis, Old Kingdom Egypt (4th Dynasty)

importance.justification: The only one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World still standing and the largest pyramid ever built.
